Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a recipe into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme recipe and deliver a live timeline: Saturday Brunch for Four for 4 people
Resource limits: one oven, two burners, one cook, about 45 minutes.
Everything must be finished by 10:00.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Saturday Brunch for Four

Everything on the table at ten. The bacon cooks in the oven so the stove is free for pancakes; the fruit salad and the coffee fill the gaps. One person can do this in about 45 minutes.

Bacon
Lay a pound of bacon on a rack over a sheet pan and bake at 400°F for 20 minutes, until crisp, turning the pan once halfway. Drain on paper towels for 2 minutes; it stays warm for a while.

Pancakes
Whisk together two cups of flour, two tablespoons of sugar, a tablespoon of baking powder and a teaspoon of salt; 5 minutes. In a jug beat two eggs with a cup and a half of milk and three tablespoons of melted butter, then stir the wet into the dry until just combined, another 5 minutes; lumps are fine. Let the batter rest for 10 minutes while the bacon cooks. Heat a griddle over medium heat for 5 minutes. Cook the pancakes in batches, a quarter cup each, about 2 minutes per side, 15 minutes for the whole batch.

Fruit salad
Halve a pint of strawberries, cube a small melon and a mango, and add a cup of blueberries; this takes about 10 minutes. Squeeze half a lime over the top and chill for at least 15 minutes.

Coffee
Grind the beans and set up the pot, 3 minutes, then brew a full pot, which takes 8 minutes, timed to finish as the pancakes come off the griddle.

Serve
Bring everything out together while the pancakes are hot; 2 minutes.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "summary": "one paragraph: what is being made, for how many, by when, under what constraints",
  "servesOrScale": "8 people",
  "deadline": "2026-11-26T18:00:00",
  "constraints": ["one oven", "two burners", "two cooks"]
}
```

Saturday Brunch for Four is a single-cook brunch for four people that needs to be fully ready to serve by 10:00, with about 45 minutes of active prep and cooking. The source text appears complete and does not seem truncated. It uses one oven for the bacon so that the two-burner stovetop stays free for the griddle/pancakes, and the schedule also has to work around rest, drain, chill, and timing requirements: the bacon drains for 2 minutes and stays warm, the pancake batter rests for 10 minutes while the bacon cooks, the fruit salad must chill for at least 15 minutes, the coffee brews for 8 minutes and is timed to finish as the pancakes come off the griddle, and everything is brought out together in a 2-minute serve while the pancakes are still hot.

```json
{
  "summary": "Saturday Brunch for Four is a one-person brunch for four guests that must be ready by 10:00 in about 45 minutes. It coordinates bacon baked in the oven, pancakes made on the stove, fruit salad that chills, and coffee timed to finish with the pancakes. Key constraints are one oven, two burners, one cook, a 10-minute batter rest, a 15-minute chill for the fruit salad, a 2-minute bacon drain, and coffee brewing in 8 minutes so it finishes as the pancakes come off the griddle, with everything served together within 2 minutes.",
  "servesOrScale": "4 people",
  "deadline": "10:00",
  "constraints": [
    "one oven",
    "two burners",
    "one cook",
    "about 45 minutes total",
    "everything finished by 10:00",
    "bacon drains on paper towels for 2 minutes",
    "pancake batter rests for 10 minutes",
    "fruit salad chills for at least 15 minutes",
    "coffee brews for 8 minutes",
    "coffee must finish as the pancakes come off the griddle",
    "serve everything together while pancakes are hot"
  ]
}
```

A track is one sequential lane of work, so steps in the same track must not overlap, while any work that needs to happen at the same time goes in a different track. Each step has exactly one duration kind: `fixed` with `seconds`, `variable` with `minSeconds`, `maxSeconds`, and usually `defaultSeconds`, or `indefinite` if it runs until the person stops it. A step’s `startTrigger` says when it begins, such as at program start, at an offset from program start, after another step, after a buffer, manually, on abort, or by a compound trigger. Every `stepId` must be unique across the entire program, not just within one track. Every `task` a step uses needs a matching `resourceConstraints` entry, and `maxConcurrent` is what models shared equipment or work space, such as one oven or two burners. If the same work is repeated `n` times, it should be modeled as `replicates` on one step, with `instances: "each"` for per-copy follow-on work, `instances: "all"` for the barrier, and `maxInFlight` when an intermediate holding area limits how many copies can be in progress.

Expected resource constraints for this brunch:

- `oven`: `maxConcurrent: 1` — only one oven; bacon uses it.
- `burner`: `maxConcurrent: 2` — two stovetop burners exist; pancake griddle is the main stove work, with spare capacity if butter or other stove items need modeling.
- `prep`: `maxConcurrent: 1` — one cook and one active working person/station for mixing, chopping, laying out bacon, and serving.
- `coffee_maker`: `maxConcurrent: 1` — one coffee pot/machine brews one pot.
- `hold`: `maxConcurrent: 3` — passive resting/drain/chilling steps may overlap, such as batter resting, bacon draining, and fruit chilling.

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "tracks are sequential lines of work; one duration kind per step; triggers link steps; stepIds are global; every task needs a resourceConstraint; repeated work uses replicates with each/all/maxInFlight.",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "oven", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "burner", "maxConcurrent": 2 },
    { "task": "prep", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "coffee_maker", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "hold", "maxConcurrent": 3 }
  ],
  "actors": 1
}
```
